name: Sable Fredriksen
location: The Shelf, Geartown, near Halsted and Division
description:
Sable Fredriksen is a big man gone soft at the edges, with the kind of weathered dark-brown face that has accumulated sixty-four years of Geartown grime into its creases. His Burkinabé father's cheekbones sit high and prominent beneath small, watchful eyes, and the Swedish side of the family gave him an improbable red-grey beard that he refuses to trim, which is now impressively large. His left arm from the elbow down is a heavy-duty industrial prosthetic in bare gunmetal — he has never decorated it, never chromed it, and finds the idea faintly obscene. He moves slowly, deliberately, like a man who has learned that things don't need to be rushed when you know what you have.

Sable Fredriksen's stall on The Shelf is less a stall than an archaeology site — forty years of accumulated junk organized according to a system that exists only in his head, which he navigates with the certainty of a man walking through his own house in the dark. He is terse with strangers, generous to a fault with regulars, and holds strong opinions about the difference between junk worth keeping and junk that has given up. He prays loudly to the ELF he believes inhabits a broken micro-fabricator at the back of his stall, which he calls 'the Sleeper,' and leaves it oiling rags as offerings.

core_fears: The stall being cleared out — either by death or by force
Geartown changing until nothing he knows is left
core_desires: To be remembered as someone who kept useful things alive
coping_mechanisms: The daily prayer ritual with the Sleeper — it gives structure
blind_spots: Mistrusts anything new or corporate by default, which occasionally means missing genuine value
Has not processed his wife's death five years ago — deflects any mention of her
psychology.secret: He found a Zheng-Dao proprietary fabrication schematic in a salvage haul two years ago — something significant enough that he knew immediately he should not have it. He has not sold it. He has not told anyone about it. It is folded inside an oiling rag that he moves to a new hiding spot in the stall every month. He doesn't know what to do with it but knows that throwing it away feels wrong.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Minimal. Short declarative sentences. Technical vocabulary for parts and salvage is precise and extensive; personal vocabulary is deliberately narrow.
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow, with long pauses that he is entirely comfortable with and other people are not
verbal_tics: 'That's not junk, that's a —' followed by a technical term
Refers to the Sleeper in conversation as if it is present and listening
example_lines: 'You want that capacitor. You don't want that capacitor. You want what that capacitor can become. Different thing.'
'Sleeper's been restless. Means something's coming through the grid. You got anything electric on you that's been glitching? Thought so. Leave it here overnight.'

story_hooks: The Zheng-Dao schematic has been quietly searched for — someone knows a copy left a specific facility, and the search has reached Geartown. Goran hasn't connected the dots yet, but someone looking closely will.
The Sleeper has been emitting a low-frequency signal that three other vendors on The Shelf have independently noticed. Goran believes it's a message. He might be right.
narrative_function: Equipment and parts source, local historian of Geartown, ELF lore through his relationship with the Sleeper. A character who has seen enough that he remembers things others have forgotten — corporate actions, neighborhood changes, people who disappeared.
augmentations: Left forearm industrial prosthetic (functional, undecorated). Subretinal low-light enhancer — 'for reading part numbers in the dark, nothing fancy.'
daily_life: Opens at dawn, when the salvage haulers come through with fresh loads. Spends mornings sorting and appraising, afternoons selling and trading, evenings doing minor repair work on salvageable items. Eats at the stall. Goes home to Geartown at dusk, walking the same route he has walked for forty years.
affiliation: Independent; long-standing member of The Shelf informal vendor collective; deep roots in the Geartown community

decision_rules: Never sell something you can't honestly describe
If something came from a corporate haul, price it double — they can afford it
escalation_ladder: A single pointed question that reframes the problem as the other person's
Standing up from his stool — this alone usually resolves most situations
The prosthetic arm, which is very heavy, set deliberately on a surface

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally minimal — prices things, answers questions, doesn't volunteer
interpersonal_modes.friends: Suddenly and unexpectedly generous, remembered preferences, awkward warmth

stress_responses.medium: Reorganizes a section of the stall with no apparent purpose
stress_responses.high: Goes very still and very quiet, which his neighbors have learned to recognize as a warning

contradictions: Believes things should be used, not hoarded — but has been sitting on the schematic for two years
Dismisses sentiment as weakness, has kept every tool his late wife ever touched
habits: Morning: tea, oiling the Sleeper's casing, price review
Evening: same walk home, stops at the same corner to look at the lake if the smog allows
Talks to the items in his stall while sorting them
breaking_points: Learning that the schematic's existence has put someone he knows in danger

timeline.event: Born in Geartown to a Burkinabé father and a Swedish-Burkinabé mother
Lost left arm below the elbow in a Geartown salvage yard accident; received industrial prosthetic through a UBC medical program
Opened the stall on The Shelf
Wife Marta died of a respiratory illness linked to Geartown industrial runoff — Goran has never pursued the corporate liability claim
Found the Zheng-Dao schematic in a salvage haul; has told no one

carried_weapons: Street Custom 'Spiderbite' Electrified Barbed Wire Launcher
related_entities: Vespid Dynamics Paralytic Aerosol Grenade PAG-2 'Sleepy Time'
Tessera Industries Quantum Entanglement Detonator QED-1 'Certainty'

physical_description.heritage: Northern European (37.3%), Hispanic/Latin American (33.1%), Southeast Asian (18.4%), and South Asian (11.2%) ancestry; creates a warm golden-brown skin tone with subtle olive undertones from the balanced, complex ancestral blend. The mix produces moderate facial structure with defined cheekbones and jawline characteristic of diverse genetic heritage.
physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and barrel-chested, softening at the waist and midsection with age; still carries the frame of a man who moved heavy things for decades, now settled into deliberate, economical movement
physical_description.hair_style: Full, unkempt beard extending to mid-chest, unstyled and never trimmed; hair on head short and thinning, greyed almost completely
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown with faint subretinal augmentation visible as a faint amber luminescence in low light
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm golden-brown with subtle olive depth, midtone from balanced ancestral blend; greyed and weathered from decades of metallic dust exposure
physical_description.complexion: Heavily lined face with deep creases around the eyes and mouth; weathered but clean; small scar through left eyebrow from a tool accident in his fifties; calloused hands, right hand more than left; facial structure shows blended ancestry with moderate cheekbones and defined jawline reflecting Northern European, Hispanic, Southeast Asian, and South Asian genetic mix
distinguishing_marks: Deep horizontal scar across the left temple, pale against golden-brown skin, approximately 4cm long from a salvage accident in his forties
Faint burn marks across the knuckles of his right hand from soldering work, barely visible unless examined closely
Tattoo on inner right forearm in faded indigo: a geometric pattern of interlocking lines and circles, old-school work from the 2180s, now blurred with age
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Left arm prosthetic from elbow down: heavy-duty industrial model in bare gunmetal grey, utilitarian and undecorated, with visible joint articulation and cable routing; no chrome, no color-work, no aesthetic modification. Subretinal augmentation not immediately obvious but produces faint amber glow in darkness when active.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves slowly and deliberately with the careful economy of an older man who has learned efficiency through forty years of repetition; stands with weight favoring right side due to left arm imbalance; rarely rushes; communicates with economy of gesture and long, appraising stares; carries himself with the quiet confidence of someone in complete command of their small domain
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4-5 practical: heavy canvas cargo pants in faded black, patched at both knees with different fabric; worn Carhartt-style jacket in brown, stained with oil and oxidation; thermal undershirt visible at neckline, greyed from washing; steel-toed boots, scuffed and re-soled multiple times; no jewelry except a simple band on right ring finger (silver, old). Everything functional, nothing decorative. No corporate branding.
